name: Engineers India Ltd
title: Engineers India Ltd - 532178 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Engineers India FY26 standalone turnover rose 27% to Rs.3,849 crore and PAT 37% to Rs.638 crore; order book hit a record Rs.15,109 crore.
summary.overview: FY26 was a record year: standalone turnover Rs.3,849 crore (+27% YoY), PAT Rs.638 crore (+37%), operating margin 16.22% (vs 14.76%), and EPS Rs.11.36 (vs Rs.8.28). Q4 turnover was Rs.899 crore with PBT Rs.195 crore and PAT Rs.152 crore. Order inflow was Rs.7,979 crore versus Rs.8,214 crore a year earlier, while the order book reached Rs.15,109 crore (Rs.11,717 crore a year earlier). Management flagged a slowdown in Middle East awards due to the regional conflict, while domestic and Africa activity was steady, and guided FY27 consultancy margins of 20-25% and LSTK margins of 5-7%.

segments.name: Consultancy & engineering
segments.commentary: FY26 turnover Rs.1,782 crore (vs Rs.1,678 crore); Q4 turnover Rs.489 crore with a reported Q4 margin near 29%, which management attributed to a Rs.221 crore change order, not a one-off write-back. Guided segment margin 20-25%.

segments.name: Turnkey (LSTK)
segments.commentary: FY26 turnover Rs.2,067 crore (vs Rs.1,349 crore); Q4 turnover Rs.410 crore. Guided segment margin 5-7%. Dangote refinery (USD 360 million) and fertilizer (USD 70 million, four lines) contracts are being executed, started around January 2026.

segments.name: Subsidiary CEIL
segments.commentary: Profit rose to Rs.24.71 crore in FY26 from Rs.20.62 crore. Associate (refinery-linked) profit was about Rs.40 crore in the latest quarter after a shutdown-affected earlier period; management expects 100% plant capacity this year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 order inflow to stay around Rs.8,000 crore (consultancy plus LSTK), with an aim to exceed it; management said FY27 inflow is hard to predict beyond one or two quarters.
FY27 revenue growth guided at a minimum of 10-15%, based on two months of the year elapsed.
Consultancy segment margin to be sustained at 20-25%; LSTK segment margin at 5-7%.
Consultancy revenue growth seen conservatively at 15-20% a year over the next two to three years.
Middle East: management expects a delay of a couple of months in big-ticket awards; Africa and the new Saudi Aramco agreements (5+3 years) are the growth routes.
Final dividend of Rs.2.5 per share proposed; with the interim Rs.2.5, total FY26 dividend is Rs.5 per share (100% of face value Rs.5).
capex_capacity: Dangote refinery and fertilizer projects are about four years in duration; site activity expected to start around end-2026 or early 2027.
Andhra (BPCL) project: feasibility underway; licensor selection next, with project activities targeted in FY27.
IOCL Paradip phase-2 balance order (about Rs.8-10 billion) expected to be awarded by end of FY27, after the investment decision.
Panipat (P25) project is in advanced construction and expected to commission soon.
Company is setting up a CBG plant in Maharashtra on its own investment and is the OT consultant for an MRPL sustainable aviation fuel plant.
demand_pricing: Order book is at a record Rs.15,109 crore, but FY26 inflow was slightly lower than FY25 at Rs.7,979 crore.
Middle East is about 30% of overseas business secured, and roughly 10-15% of the current order book. Big-ticket Middle East awards are slower, with client decisions delayed by security concerns.
Africa is the main overseas focus after the Dangote awards; management sees investment shifting to Africa as an alternative hub.
Infrastructure is about 25% of FY26 order inflow (clients include ONGC, NTPC, Government of Rajasthan, IIMs/IITs and data centres).
Coal gasification: government raised viability gap funding; a consultancy opportunity of about Rs.300-400 crore was indicated. Project sizes of Rs.10,000-40,000 crore were cited.
Public-sector tenders are competitive or negotiated; hit rate on bids is about 20-25%. Nomination only for critical projects.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for FY27 consultancy inflow in domestic and international markets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to sustain inflow at roughly the current level of about Rs.8,000 crore total; Middle East slowdown is the key risk, with domestic projects not being delayed or cancelled.

qa_highlights.question: Middle East share of the order book and outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Middle East is about 30% of overseas business secured and 10-15% of the current order book; a Saudi Aramco long-term agreement (5+3 years) was signed, with an out-of-kingdom agreement pending.

qa_highlights.question: Was there any one-off or change order behind Q4 consultancy margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there were no write-offs; a Rs.221 crore change order was received in FY26 and the expenditure already incurred, and the Q4 margins are described as normalised.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue slippage Q4 vs Q3 and cost pressures?
qa_highlights.answer: No revenue slippage; the prior quarter included a change order over Rs.200 crore, which made it high-profit. Management did not report commodity cost impacts.

qa_highlights.question: Expected growth in FY27 revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Minimum 10-15% growth expected in FY27 execution; FY27 and FY28 revenue guidance was deferred to next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Middle East and Africa opportunity size?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Rs.1,000-2,000 crore of projects is achievable over time, with an inflection expected around FY27-FY29.

risks_watch: Middle East conflict delaying big-ticket awards and revamp-led spending; monitor Saudi and out-of-kingdom agreement signing.
Consultancy order inflow, with FY26 slightly below FY25 and the Rs.8,000 crore FY27 target dependent on public-sector tenders.
Sustainability of 20%+ consultancy margins; Q4 margin benefited from a Rs.221 crore change order.
Dangote and IOCL Paradip conversion timing; large LSTK jobs carry 5-7% margins.
Associate plant operating at full capacity this year after a prior shutdown.
Disclosure readability: an analyst flagged that the figures uploaded to the exchanges are hard to read.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the domestic book and FY26 results, but cautious and hedged on the Middle East and on FY27 inflow, repeatedly saying 'let us hope' and 'too early' to answer questions on timelines and sizes.
key_quotes: Company order book position has reached its all-time high and stands at Rs.15,109 crores as on 31st March 2026, as compared to Rs.11,717 crores as on 31st March 2025.
We are continuously maintaining our consultancy margin in the range of 20% to 25% percent and in the LSTK business around 5% to 7%.
There is no nomination cases are coming from the public sector unless there is a very critical project or there is nobody in the industry who can do it.
But we have not seen in the domestic market anywhere any project being delayed or anything being done.

financial_highlights.value: Rs.899 crore (consultancy Rs.489 crore, turnkey Rs.410 crore)

financial_highlights.change: vs Rs.11,717 crore a year earlier

growth.why: FY27 revenue guided at minimum 10-15% (midpoint 12.5%), backed by a record Rs.15,109 crore order book and margin guidance, while FY27 order inflow is held at about Rs.8,000 crore versus Rs.7,979 crore in FY26 and Middle East big-ticket awards are slowing.
